headline: 1 master validator app (ID 2714516089) on Algorand catalogued; child pool contracts are factory-spawned (count unknown); on-chain reads blocked — DeFiPunkd API does not support Algorand.
short_headline: 1 master app + N factory pools on Algorand

findings.text: D1: Algorand is not an EVM chain; canonical explorers (etherscan, basescan, etc.) do not apply. Algorand's Pera Explorer and AlgoExplorer were identified via search but not fetched due to fetch-limit constraints. No hex address name-tag search was possible; Algorand uses numeric Application IDs. The master validator App ID 2714516089 was confirmed from the official docs page (txnlab.gitbook.io), not from an explorer fetch.

D2: Official deployment info found at https://txnlab.gitbook.io/reti-open-pooling/technical-implementation/smart-contracts.md (fetched). States 'Mainnet app id is: 2714516089'. No separate deployed-contracts page exists beyond this; the smart-contracts doc page is the canonical deployment reference.

D3: Audit link https://github.com/algorandfoundation/reti/tree/main/contracts/contracts/audit confirmed in both the docs page and protocol.audit_links. GitHub fetch was blocked (permission denied), so no audit PDF scope table could be extracted. Audit firm and date remain unknown from this run.

D4: GitHub repo https://github.com/algorandfoundation/reti confirmed from search results. Direct fetch of GitHub was blocked ('You don't have permission to access this domain'). No broadcast JSON, hardhat-deploy artifacts, or deployment index files could be read. Pinned commit SHA not obtainable this run.
D5: Protocol is single-chain (Algorand only). No multi-chain enumeration required. D5 not applicable beyond confirming single-chain scope.

D6: Architecture confirmed via docs: the master ValidatorContract (App ID 2714516089) acts as a factory that creates child staking pool contracts from a pre-defined template. Child pool enumeration not possible this run — DeFiPunkd read API does not support Algorand (not in supported chainIds: 1, 10, 56, 130, 137, 324, 8453, 42161, 43114, 59144, 81457, 534352, 11155111). consensus.algorand.observer search snippet reports Reti pools hold ~726.5M ALGO (~36.8% of online stake), indicating many active child pools. Cap notice: child pool count unknown; factory App ID 2714516089 is the enumeration entry point.

D7: Role taxonomy applied. App ID 2714516089 classified as 'factory' (master validator contract that creates child pools) and 'other' (primary protocol entry point for staking). Child pool contracts classified as 'pool' — factory-spawned, each a distinct Algorand application account. Actor class is 'unknown' for all — no on-chain bytecode read was possible this run.

D8: App ID 2714516089 traces to fetched URL https://txnlab.gitbook.io/reti-open-pooling/technical-implementation/smart-contracts.md. All entries in admin_addresses[] backed by this fetched source. No snippet-only sightings promoted without fetch evidence.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run on a single-chain Algorand protocol. The master validator contract (App ID 2714516089) was catalogued from the fetched official docs page. Child pool contracts are factory-spawned and cannot be enumerated without Algorand-native tooling — DeFiPunkd's read API does not support Algorand. GitHub was fetch-blocked, preventing audit scope extraction and deployment artifact walking. grade=unknown because on-chain state reads were not achievable and the address book was empty at run start.

protocol_metadata.about: Réti Open Pooling is a decentralized, non-custodial staking pool protocol on the Algorand network that allows users to pool ALGO stake in order to meet the minimum threshold required for consensus participation and node rewards. Users direct stake to a validator via a master ValidatorContract (App ID 2714516089), which factory-spawns child staking pool contracts — each operating as a distinct Algorand account eligible for consensus. Validators earn a configurable commission per epoch, while stakers receive compounded rewards automatically proportional to their contribution. The protocol is open-source, written in TEALScript/AlgoKit, and has been commercially audited.
